To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transparency is an essential feature of social coding platforms such as GitHub, and it is used by users for a range of social and technical purposes.

GitHub users make a surprising number of social inferences about each other based on activity data in the system, which they combine into effective social coding strategies that improve their work and their reputation.

GitHub users use the social coding platform to: 1. coordinate their technical work; 2. learn new skills from other developers' code; 3. manage their professional reputation; 4. build social capital with other developers; and 5. find new projects to work on.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how social information is used to make decisions in a large-scale distributed collaboration, and how these decisions affect the structure of the collaboration.
how people use social information to manage their participation in a large-scale, networked community of practice.
the role of transparency in the social coordination of work and learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transparency in GitHub has a strong positive effect on the collaboration and learning of software developers, but the effect is highly variable across different users and different situations.
transparency is an important and valuable aspect of GitHub, but that it is not always used in a positive way.
the social coding in GitHub is not only transparent but also collaborative.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transparency and openness of the social coding platform GitHub has led to a rich and diverse set of social infor- mation that users leverage to make social inferences and coordinate their work.
social coding in GitHub is a form of social media that is highly effective at coordinating and supporting large-scale distributed collaboration.
GitHub is not just a tool for code sharing and version control, but a platform for a wide variety of social interactions that are crucial to the success of open source projects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transparency in the form of publicly available activity data can provide an effective basis for social coordination and collaboration.
transparency is not just about making information public, it is also about making it meaningful.
transparency can be a powerful social tool for coordinating complex work.
